plain.title: Start the answer with a three-token cue ending in "Okay"
plain.what: The base model's answer is started for it with a cue: three tokens ending in the word "Okay", copied from the way the RL-trained model opens its own answers. Nothing else changes. Right answers go from 224 to 410 of 500.

nodes.text: Wang et al. 2610.06851, read in full (papers/arxiv-2610.06851.txt). (1) Their RL model is allenai/Olmo-3-7B-RL-Zero-Math (3.0 release, per their repo), not our Olmo-3.1. On MATH-500 at T 0.6 / top-p 0.95 / cap 31,744, 32 rollouts: base 42.2 -> cue 77.9 (Table 5); RL 75.0 -> 75.3 with cue (Table 6). So on their pair the cue already equals RL on MATH-500; our 10.6-point gap is against 3.1 only and is not in the paper. (2) DIRECTION.md says they report 77.7 for the cue: Table 5 says 77.9; 77.7 is the row 'RL opening + base continuation' (Table 13). (3) Their cue is 2 tokens ('.\n\n' + 'Okay'), chosen without labels by lowest answer entropy on 30 MATH train problems. (4) Cued base pass@16 on MATH-500 = 95.4 (Table 5), above our RL pass@1 of 92.6: the missing points are in the base's samples. (5) Harder sets: RL leads the cued base by 5-12 points (AMC 23 66.2 vs 59.5, AIME 2024 35.2 vs 23.3, OlympiadBench 41.6 vs 36.5), unexplained in the paper. (6) Not in the paper: any temperature sweep, restarts, base + a*(RL - base), a Code-RL model. 0 citing papers indexed on 2026-11-14. (7) Olmo 3 report 2512.13961 A.6.4: 3.1 differs from 3.0 by completion length 16k instead of 12k and by not masking truncated sequences (they are trained as negatives). work-2aaf3a

Published, do not run on a plain base (papers read in full, texts in papers/): (a) power sampling / MCMC: +2.4 to +3.5 points on MATH-500, 18-27 % of the RL gain, none on AIME (2610.24663 Table 1). (b) Fixed rules: forced 'Wait', logit bias, greedy first 100 tokens, entropy stop, longer prefill: at or below base (2610.24663 Tables 3, 5, App. G). (c) Majority vote: plain base stays below RL for 24 of 24 decoding policies at every N up to 16 on Qwen2.5-7B / MATH-500 (2609.01274 Fig. 8b). Maj@4 adds 0.8 points to a 73.6 % model on MATH500; best-of-n by self-confidence is below one sample (2507.18122 Table 1). (d) Loop penalties: DRY costs 14.2 points on MATH-500 for Qwen3-4B (2610.24715 Table 16). (e) Top-p vs temperature: removing top-p at T 0.6 cuts limit loops 59 -> 53, T 1 cuts to 24 (Qwen3-4B, 360 structured generations, not math; 2610.24715 Table 9). (f) RL gain is sparse: RL's greedy token at the 4 % of positions where greedy tokens differ recovers 90.5 % of the gain on AIME; base entropy finds those positions with AUROC 0.94-0.98; RL's token has mean rank 2.1-2.4 in the base (2610.24663 Table 3, App. E; 2605.06241 Table 2). No label-free rule is published that picks the right token there. (g) Label-free training (entropy minimization, vote reward) closes 80-100 % of the gap on Math-500 and 0-70 % on AIME for Qwen2.5-Math-7B (2505.15134 Table 2); vote reward collapses near 1,000 steps (2603.08660). None of (a)-(g) was run on a cued base or on the Olmo pair. work-2aaf3a

T1 data: base answers of <= 2,000 tokens are 263 of 500 and 13 are wrong; RL has 0 wrong among its 286 answers of <= 4,000 tokens. Procedure: when the first answer is <= 2,000 tokens, draw a second sample; if the two final answers differ, draw a third and take the majority. Cost ~514 extra tokens per problem, so base stays under RL's mean (3,933 + 514 vs 4,694). RL gets the same procedure (expected gain 0). Closest published: Maj@2/4 in 2507.18122 Table 1 and majority@k in 2610.06851 Fig. 21; differs in gating by length, matching tokens to RL, cued base. Refuted if fewer than 8 of the 13 are recovered (errors repeat across samples) or new errors offset them. Then the 328. From work-2aaf3a.

Goodfire 'Neurons as an Interpretable Basis' (Nov 10 2026, goodfire.com/research/neurons-as-an-interpretable-basis), read in full by a subagent. Table 1/8 on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (MoE, SwiGLU): keeping only the top 320 of 4,096 routed MLP neuron activations per token and layer, with no training, raises loss 1.886 -> 1.940 (+2.9%) and raises MATH-500 from 69.8 by +5.8 (top-64: +7.0; resample noise +0.8) at a 4,096 thinking-token cap. Accuracy on items both arms finished is flat, so the gain is more answers finishing under the cap (subagent's inference). Other evals fell (GPQA-Diamond -11 to -18, MBPP+ -20) from looping and excess self-checking. Fig. 4: ablating all Q3 activations (gate<0 and up<0) cut GSM8K reasoning 1,550 -> 176 tokens. Single neurons control 'settle vs keep questioning' (L9_E98_N330). Their small RL recalibration 'mainly taught the model to commit and stop'. Not in the paper: any base-vs-fine-tune diff, any weight edit, any model near 7B. No code released.

Neuron-level route, literature state (19 Exa searches, 12 full reads, 2026-11-14): no paper diffs a base against its RL version in the MLP-neuron basis, transplants the top neurons and scores reasoning. For sparsity: Lu et al. 2611.10866, a reward-trained mask zeroing <0.05% of MLP gate weights matches full fine-tune (Qwen2.5-7B mean 52.3 vs 51.9, base 40.2; untrained Wanda mask at most 42.5); EdgeRunner 2606.13705, 1 to 1,062 neurons cut loops 46/384 -> 12/384 at T 0.7 with no measured regression; AdaRAS 2601.19847, label-ranked neuron steering MATH-500 84.8 -> 86.4. Against: Mukherjee 2505.11711, RL updates spread over all layers and matrices, near full rank; 2611.11752, OLMo-2-7B PPO update needs 2,120 of 4,096 components for 80% energy at L16 down-proj. Arora et al. 2601.22594 (RelP attribution, code github.com/TransluceAI/circuits): ~200 neurons give a faithful circuit for single-token tasks on Llama 3.1 8B. Local: studies/rlneurons/lib/n13_arms.py already builds neuron-transplant checkpoints (top 0.1/0.3/1/3% most-changed neurons moved to RL, energy-matched random controls, MLP-only, attention-only); the ranking driver and all arm scores are missing. Olmo 3 7B: 32 layers x 11,008 SwiGLU neurons = 352,256.

Disagreement map, MATH-500, 500 T1 (base+cue) + 500 T2 (RL) answers scored under both Olmo models: the hypothesis 'RL refuses the token where the base starts a quick wrong answer' is REFUTED. D = ln P_RL - ln P_base at the base's answer-start token: wrong answers under 4,000 tokens median -0.53 (n=21), right answers of <= 2,000 tokens median -0.21 (n=250), permutation p = 0.82. D follows the answer format, not correctness: 'Answer:' line median -8.36 (n=132, 121 right), \boxed 0.000 (n=338); RL gives a wrong box the base's probability (median D 0.001, n=10). Top-1 tokens differ at 7.98 % of 1,966,404 T1 positions and 8.20 % of 2,346,899 T2 positions; the top 4 % of positions carry 38.7 % of KL (not sparse as in the 1-4 % published for greedy rollouts on Qwen pairs). Mean KL per token after the cue 0.06-0.09 nats; cue positions 8-12 nats. On the 16 cap hits RL's largest gaps are early (median relative position 0.19) and prefer ' Wait', ' too', ' Hmm'. At the base's true ends RL's P(stop) is below 0.5 in 16.5 % of 473 answers (base 4.2 %). Controls passed (base vs base KL 0, cue positions, calibration). nodes.text: cleanneurons Part T (transplant curve), Olmo 3 base vs RL-Zero-Math, teacher-forced on 80 stored MATH-500 answers (40 T1, 40 T2), 131,237 positions after the cue: the RL change is NOT concentrated in MLP neurons. Copying the top 1 % of neurons by weight change (3,523 of 352,256) from RL into the base closes 3.9 % (T1 text) and 5.7 % (T2 text) of KL(RL||base) at the 4 % most-different positions; a random 1 % closes 0.7-0.9 %. Top 10 %: 14.7 / 20.3 % (random 7.0 / 9.7); top 30 %: 28.3 / 42.7 % (random 20.0 / 31.2). All MLP neurons: 69.4 / 85.8 %; all attention projections: 50.4 / 67.7 %; norms+embeddings: 4.0 / 4.6 %. MLP layers 0-15 carry about twice what 16-31 do. Weight change is flat: each layer 3.0-3.2 % of the MLP change, top 1 % of neurons hold 1.5 %. Hypothesis 'top 1 % closes >= 50 %' refuted. Controls passed (all-tensors KL 0, undo bit-exact, unedited arm = base). Limit: distance to RL, not accuracy; ranking by weight change only, attribution ranking is next. From interp_research instruments E2 (a check of the Weight-Space Programming loop edit, complements knowledge-c9fc18 and result-6199f4): we re-ran the released Qwen3.5-0.8B edit (the editor's direction projected out of 64 MLP-out columns in each of layers 15 and 19, strength 6) beside random-column controls. 300 MATH-500 problems, one sample, 8,192-token cap, presence penalty 1.5. Accuracy: base 14/300 (4.7 %), released edit 33/300 (11.0 %), one random column set matched on weight norm 28/300 (9.3 %), one matched on KL 30/300 (10.0 %). Edit minus norm-matched random: +1.7 points [-1.7, +5.0], not separated. Cap hits: base 95 %, edit 88 %, random 90 %. The edit is specific on loops: the share of answers with a repeated 10-gram falls by 0.317 [0.247, 0.383] under the edit and by 0.08-0.09 under random columns. Columns ranked by alignment with the editor's direction reproduce it (64 columns 0.307, 256 columns 0.377), but that direction is the edit's own singular vector, so no weights-only discovery is shown. A KL-matched random control was no stricter than a norm-matched one. Status: exploratory; the frozen room gate cancelled every rule (cut share 0.96; the editor's own 32,768-token eval also cuts 93 % of base answers); one random draw only. Lesson for base + a*(RL - base) (work-d36669): on a cap-limited model a random edit of matched norm can give most of an accuracy gain; report a random-direction arm, cap hits and loops beside accuracy. Artifact: interp_research studies/reproductions/instruments_e2/results/verdict_e2.json (reported.per_arm); studies/instruments/results/RESULTS.md Results 22-27.

cleanneurons Part T2 (attribution-ranked transplant), Olmo 3 base vs RL-Zero-Math: ranked by effect on 40 stored answers and scored on 40 held-out ones (2,672 decisive positions after the cue), the best 1 % of MLP neurons (3,523) copied from RL closes 13.7 % (T1 text) / 18.6 % (T2 text) of KL(RL||base); weight-change ranking 4.2 / 5.8 %, random 0.7 / 1.0 %. Best 0.1 % (352 neurons): 5.4 / 7.3 %. Best 10 %: 33.6 / 48.9 %. All MLP: 67.7 / 86.4 %. 88 % of all 352,256 neurons have a positive score, and the effects add up linearly: summed first-order scores predict a 0.542-nat drop, copying all MLP neurons gives 0.549 (of 0.708). So RL is a small, nearly linear nudge to almost every neuron; no small neuron set carries it, though the head is heavy (top 1 % = 19 % of the score). The best set sits in layers 1-15 (381 of 3,523 in layer 9) and layer 31. Hypothesis 'best 1 % closes >= 30 %' not met. Controls passed. Limit: teacher-forced distance to RL, not accuracy. nodes.text: From interp_research instruments (E1, E1b, E5, E6b; complements work-383069 and result-156f7b): on Olmo-3-1025-7B, writing a replacement value into a set of ~50 earlier-layer MLP neurons also moves a target neuron on contexts unrelated to that set, an off-target term absent in gemma and Qwen. Measured with 56 fake two-neuron pairs as the ratio of off-target fall to own fall (null should be 0): mean replacement 0.163 with all neurons eligible, 0.067 [0.034, 0.089] with the always-on neurons excluded; zero with exclusion 0.007 [-0.002, 0.032]; median 0.049; resample 0.147 (worst). Own falls are 0.42-0.48 under every value, so the value choice moves only the off-target part. gemma-3-4b-pt 0.004 and Qwen3-4B-Base 0.003 (no term). OLMo-2-1124-7B 0.123 [0.087, 0.169] against Olmo-3's 0.128 like for like: the term belongs to the OLMo lineage, not to Olmo-3's training run. Candidate causes, not separated: no input norms (output norms only), QK-norm over the whole projection, d 4096, MHA, untied embeddings. The term travels through the other window positions: writing only at the measured token leaves 0.005 [0.002, 0.010] against 0.074. Always-on neurons = top 1 % by mean activation (3,412); the ones that act are a few dozen mid-layer outliers at ~145x their layer's median |activation|. Rule for Olmo-3: zero (or write at the measured token only) with always-on neurons excluded; never mean replacement; on any OLMo model measure a random-set null first. Ablation results from Qwen or gemma papers do not transfer to Olmo without that null. Status: closed 2026-11-05, every stage read by a different model (errata E1b-b, E1b-f, E5-b, E6b-a to h). Artifact: interp_research studies/instruments/results/RESULTS.md Results 4-8, 18-19, 28-34; e1/verdict_e1.json, e1b/verdict_e1b.json, e5/verdict_e5.json, e6/verdict_e6b.json.

From interp_research mechanics (Olmo-3 internals; complements work-383069, relevant to the base's loops at T 0.6 in result-dadeec): on Olmo-3-1025-7B final weights, 512 repeated random-token sequences, 1,336 MLP neurons rise on the second pass by at least 0.2 of their 99.9th-percentile scale and 1,237 fall by as much (null max 0.055), about 2,600 of 352,256. 99.5 % sit at or after layer 7, the first induction-head layer (top detector head L15 H5); counts peak at layers 10-15 (121-171 per layer) with a second group of 60 in layers 29-31. Removing the top 8 induction heads leaves 0.771 [0.706, 0.839] of the top-100 neurons' repeat response (8 random heads leave 0.980), so the response is spread over more than 8 heads. The top-100 neurons' strongest corpus passages are literal repeats (text, code, repeated row formats) 8x [4, 12] as often as layer-matched random neurons' (0.16 vs 0.02). On rare random tokens the median neuron runs at 0.72 of its natural-text activity: 2.96x in layers 0-1, 0.36x in layers 26-31. Open: repetition not yet separated from predictability (erratum O-b; the control forward never ran). Status: closed; frozen R1 holds, R2 refuted on its point value, R3 holds, R4 cancelled (no room). Use: a ready list of repeat-reading neurons to test as loop units, an alternative to ranking by weight change. Artifact: interp_research studies/mechanics/results/RESULTS.md Results 1-8; results/screen/1/verdict_mechanics.json, signatures.npz.

From interp_research neuronoff (single-neuron ablation effect sizes; complements work-383069): zeroing one MLP neuron at one sign of its activation in Qwen3-4B-Base (156 neurons) and gemma-3-4b-pt (202) moves NLL on that neuron's own top contexts by a median 0.0026-0.0093 nats per side; the per-context median is at most 0.000037 nats. Zeroing a whole layer moves the median context by 0.014 (Qwen) and 0.021 (gemma) nats. The per-neuron positive control (a 0.05-nat floor) failed on 65/156 and 75/202 neurons, so every label was cancelled. Behaviour test on 7 hand-picked neurons: 0 of 7 changed generated text when zeroed. Status: closed and reviewed (a different model recomputed it from raw banks); cancelled by its own gate. Lesson: one neuron's necessity is about 0.01 nats on its own contexts, below a per-neuron floor of 0.05; a neuron-level test on Olmo-3 needs a pooled positive control checked for room, at least 30 held-out contexts per neuron, and the Olmo off-target null (instruments item). Artifact: interp_research studies/neuronoff/CLOSEOUT.md (claims N2, N12, N13), results/RESULTS.md section 3.

Setup: MATH-500, n=500, 1 sample, T 0.6 / top-p 0.95, cap 16,384, plain prompt in chat template, grader v1 (rlneurons lib/n13_score). Endpoints base 57.2, RL 92.0 (grader v3 on the same answers: 305 and 464/500). Arms copy part of the RL-minus-base delta into the base; non-MLP tensors stay base unless named.
- Top-k most-changed MLP neurons (k = 0.1/0.3/1/3 % of 352,256): 57.6, 61.4, 61.8, 63.8.
- Random neurons scaled to the top set's change energy: 58.8, 59.8, 59.2, 63.8; random neurons at natural scale: 59.4, 58.0, 60.0, 62.8. Top minus random -1.8 to +3.4, smallest BH p 0.107.
- DARE (each MLP delta entry kept with prob q = 0.1-3 %, scaled 1/q = 1,000.7 to 33.3): 85.2, 86.8, 85.8, 86.2; second draw at 1 %: 87.8. Top minus DARE -27.6 to -22.4, BH p <= 2.6e-21.
- Whole MLP delta alone 86.4; attention + norm delta alone 83.0 (the +3.4 difference lies entirely in cap-hit problems).
- RL model with only the top-k neurons reset to base: 90.4, 90.8, 91.6, 90.6.
- GSM8K held out (n=1,319) at 1 %: top minus DARE -23.7 [-26.5, -21.1]; DARE 1 % 89.8 vs RL 92.3.
- Every arm that recovers accuracy also takes RL's format and length: 'Answer:' line in 0-4 % of answers vs 39-46 % for base-like arms; mean tokens 4,333-4,671 vs 3,133-4,004.

For the team: (1) knowledge-9d0f85 says the n13 arm scores are missing; they exist here, with accuracy, matching the KL curve in result-156f7b. (2) DARE's realized change energy is 33 to 1,000 times the whole delta's, yet it scores like the whole MLP delta: the gain tolerates large unbiased noise along the delta, so the a-sweep in work-d36669 may show a wide plateau. (3) Every recovering arm is longer: count tokens beside accuracy. Cost 102.6 GPU-h on L40S. Spec: studies/next/07_PICKS/N13_SPEC.md.

nodes.text: From interp_research bytegraft (scaling and sparse copies of a fine-tune weight difference; complements work-d36669, result-156f7b, work-f374ef): models Bolmo-1B-Stage1 (S), Bolmo-1B (F, S fine-tuned, has the skill) and OLMo-2-0425-1B (O); S's transformer body equals O's on all 176 tensors. Task: CUTE word and character edits, 1,200 items, exact match. (1) Dose curve O + lambda*(F - S) on the body, lambda 0.1 to 1.5: 23.50, 24.50, 25.25, 25.75, 27.08, 28.08, 28.75, 28.75, 27.92, 26.00 (lambda 1.0), 23.50, 15.75, 6.92, 3.75, 0.67 (O alone 22.00). Peak at lambda 0.7-0.8, not 1; past 1.1 the model collapses, and early end-of-text stops rise 5 (lambda 0.1) -> 152 (0.8) -> 181 (1.2). On S, lambda 0.5 gives 31.5 against S 23.83 and F 54.33 (25 % of the gain at half the dose). Lambda was picked on the scored items. (2) Sparse copies fail: a random 1 % of the difference scaled x100 and a random 0.1 % scaled x1000 (DARE-style) give 0/1,200; the 131 and 1,311 most-changed neurons with F's values give 22.67 and 20.00, below S's 23.83; random neurons dosed to the same realized change 24.08 and 9.42. Every entry moved: 52 of 805,306,368 body MLP entries are bit-equal, 0.095 % within 1e-5. (3) Attention vs MLP, log-odds of the gold byte at S's first wrong byte (317 items): attention difference alone +0.06 [-0.09, 0.24], MLP alone +1.81, whole body +3.00, interaction +1.13: the attention change works only together with the MLP change. An earlier accuracy reading of the split was a threshold artifact. (4) Adding the difference into a host unrelated to S (a checkpoint with weight cosine to O within +-0.002) gives 0.000 and degenerate text: adding a difference to an unrelated host breaks it and is not a transfer test (AUDIT d 8.7). Status: closed, exploratory readings, audited (AUDIT_2026-11-11d, AUDIT h2 bootstrap-seed fix). Supervised fine-tune at 1B, not RL. Artifact: interp_research studies/bytegraft/JOURNAL.md entries o_transfer_3 and A17; results/arms_1m/arms_1m.json; results/body_split_logodds/body_split_logodds.json; results/audit_2026-11-11d/audit_diff1.json.

WSP-1 anatomy (weights only, 355 tensors): RL-Math delta = 0.24% of weight norm, same in every layer; 11.8% of its squared norm sits in 8 singular directions per matrix (Gaussian null 0.5-0.8%). Late-MLP top directions x base lm_head read as deliberation words: L29 down_proj 'Okay, consider' vs 'perhaps, maybe'; 'WAIT, wait'; cue token in top 15 for 13 of 96 late readouts (RL-Code delta 15 of 96, Think-SFT 0 of 96, null 0 of 30). cos(RL-Math, RL-Code) 0.016 = 120 null sd; cos(RL-Math, Think-SFT) -0.00001: the imitation delta (24.8% of norm, 100x larger) does not point along RL. From interp_research bytegraft (how small a fitted patch carries a skill, and whether an LLM editor finds it; complements result-6199f4 and knowledge-c9fc18): S = Bolmo-1B-Stage1 lacks a CUTE word-edit skill that its fine-tune Bolmo-1B has. On 2,400 held-out check items (S 14.42): a rank-1 LoRA fitted on all 112 matrices (753,664 numbers) reads 32.04 and beats an LLM editor's 8.5M-number neuron patch by +6.50 [4.83, 8.21]. LLM editor against a gradient-ranked neuron set of matched size: -0.75 [-2.71, 1.21]. At about 1M neurons the gradient ranking reads 22.12 and random neurons 18.08. The editor's +1.42 lead over a scripted top-32 falls to +0.46 [-0.71, 1.62] at a matched seed. LLM agents choosing attention heads to patch: 0.394 and 0.363 against gradient ranking 0.356 and a script given the same evidence table 0.375. No LLM-editor advantage over a gradient ranking or a script is shown; the gain comes from fitting, not from the chosen support: F's values copied onto the editor's or the gradient ranking's support with no fit lower the host (16.42 and 17.92 against 22.00). Character edits stay at 10 % or below under every patch. Transfer trap: a patch fitted without F still raises OLMo-2-0425-1B by +8.00, so 'patch transfers to another host' measured the shared interface, not the skill. Activation transfer: writing F's attention outputs into S recovers 0.81 of F's advantage (F's MLP writes none); controls (no-skill donor scaled to F's size 0.195, another item's writes 0.031) pass, but this is the donor running in parallel, not a weight graft. Status: closed, owner's verdict 'just LoRA'; audits AUDIT f, g, h, h2. Lesson for the RL gap: report a fitted low-rank arm and a gradient-ranked arm before crediting any hand- or LLM-chosen patch. Artifact: interp_research studies/bytegraft/results/arms_1m/arms_1m.json, GRAFT_closed.md, WRITEUP_2026-11-12.md, AUDIT_2026-11-11f.md to AUDIT_2026-11-12h2.md.

From interp_research next (20_ABSTRACT.md, 'The highest-leverage next step'; not run): rank test of the RL delta. For each MLP matrix of Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math minus Olmo-3-1025-7B, add a rank-r truncation (SVD; r = 16, 64, 256) to the base, against a random subspace of equal rank and equal energy, MATH-500 (here: T 1.0, cue, run_cell.py; MLP-only so it compares with N13's whole-MLP arm, 86.4 at T 0.6), GSM8K held out on the rank-64 pair. Hypothesis: the gain sits in a low-rank part of each matrix's change (rank-64 within 2 SE of the whole-MLP arm). Refuted if rank-64 scores at the random-subspace control. Why now: N13 (knowledge-8229be) showed no neuron subset carries the gain but a 0.1 % DARE sample does; rank separates 'low-rank' from 'spread evenly'. Practical if it holds: r x (d+n) numbers per matrix for transplant or merging with the Code-RL delta. Cost estimate in the file: 6 arms, 12-16 GPU-h on L40S under N13's harness (SVD not costed); the same 6 arms on Modal H100 at T 1.0 are each one MATH-500 cell. Critique: priors point against low rank in energy (2505.11711: update nearly full rank; 2611.11752: OLMo-2-7B PPO update needs 2,120 of 4,096 components for 80 % energy at L16 down-proj), but energy rank is not functional rank, and 2605.21468 reports rank-1 trajectory extrapolation works. Also cited in interp_research next/04_RECENT.md, abstracts only: 2610.22438 (counted rank of 13 released fine-tuning updates up to 8B is only a little below a random matrix of the same shape) and 2609.22146 GRRR (removing the change of singular values keeps most math gains). WSP-1 (work-f374ef) computes singular spectra but does not score truncations. Use stochastic rounding into bf16 (work-d36669 found 54 % of delta entries <= 1 bf16 ulp).

From interp_research jmech (README.md, SPEC.md, results/run2/metrics.json): on the Olmo-3-1025-7B base, a J-lens swap of an entity written in the prompt works almost as well as editing the text, when clamped over a layer band. Status: open, not audited (no second reader).

Setup: model a81bae42, fp32; lens neuronpedia/jacobian-lens @d2527c3c (the file in knowledge-0220f1; its config sets no target layer, so it targets the final block). 8 countries x 4 relations (capital, language, continent, currency), prompts like 'Fact about {France}: the capital city of this country is'; 540 in-context terms. Edit = replace country s's two lens coordinates with country t's.
- Swap at every position, clamped over layers 12-29: the new country's answer rises 15.31 logits; replacing the word in the text gives 16.83 (91 %). Matched-norm random direction: 0.03 logits. Top-1 flips to t's answer in 519/540.
- Single-layer edit at the country token only: 5.83 logits at layer 6, 4.90 at L10, 4.46 at L14, 2.12 at L18, 0.35 at L22, 0.04 at L26 (of 32). Later positions have read the country by about layer 20.
- Not context-specific: the attributes the prompt does not ask for rise 0.56-0.60 times as much as the asked one (95 % CI about +-0.02, frozen label MIXED). Editing the text gives 0.53.
- The gradient (first-order) prediction holds only for small edits: ratio predicted/actual 0.76 (r 0.98) at strength 0.25, 0.10 (r 0.39) at strength 1.

For the team: the 'lens writes weakly' figure in result-da11d0 is for added vectors; replacing coordinates over a band of 18 layers moves a token-level variable almost fully. Set injection strength by measurement, not from the gradient. Cost: two runs of about 13 min on one RTX 6000 Ada, 0.54 USD (infra/vast/operations/2026-11-12_jmech.md).

From interp_research jmech (README.md; e2, e3, e4, e5, e6 results/run*/metrics.json): on the Olmo-3-1025-7B base, a few attention heads read an entity, and directions taken from data edit them where J-lens directions do not. Status: open, not audited. Same model, lens and country prompts as knowledge-61acfa; 1,024 heads; patch = the value a head reads from the country token, swapped to another country's.
- E2: 4 heads (L21H18, L17H2, L25H3, L18H18) give 0.82 of the all-heads effect on held-out pairs; 8 heads 0.95; 32 heads 1.00 (32 random heads, same layers: 97.5th pct 0.47). All-heads patch 16.90 logits vs 16.54 for editing the text (same held-out terms). The same heads carry world cities and US states (label SHARED). E3: same picture when the country is not written but inferred (4 heads 0.85).
- E2 weights-only head score built from fitted J-lens vectors: top-32 heads give 0.95; the same score with J = identity (unembedding rows) 0.33, with a rotated J 0.0004.
- E6, 6 content kinds (country, US state, copied word, number in a sum, word sentiment/antonym, singular/plural agreement): the lens score LOSES in 6 of 6 to a published weights-only score; the name-mover copy score (2211.00593) is best in all 6; MAPS (2412.11965) also run. The lens score names heads only for the two entity kinds (NOT NAMED for the other 4).
- E5, weight edit: projecting a direction out of the value weights of the top heads. Data direction (country-token mean minus other countries' mean, 20 sentences each): 4 heads remove 46.9 points of target-country accuracy, 8 heads 68.75 points, other countries 0 points, perplexity +0.05 %. J-lens direction on the same heads: 0 points, as does a rotated direction. Hooks removing the lens direction at layers 12-29: 0 points, perplexity +11.7 %. Reproduces Guo et al. 2410.12949.
- E4: half of a swap's effect at the last position spreads over a median 10,254 of 231,168 later MLP neurons and 6 heads; the top 100 neurons overlap lens-scored neurons 2.8 % vs 2.7 % for a rotated lens.
For the team: for the label-free direction edits (idea-d3034d), mean-difference directions edited in value weights are the tested route; J-lens directions removed nothing. In any J-lens head ranking (work-50d329), compare against the copy score. Cost 7 runs, about 4.5 USD (infra/vast/operations/2026-11-12_jmech*.md).

From interp_research rlneurons (RLN-1): RL barely moves which tokens a neuron fires on most. For each MLP neuron pole (704,512 poles = 352,256 SwiGLU neurons x 2 signs, input of down_proj), the 50 corpus positions with the strongest activation were compared between models on a fixed 20.6M-token pretraining-like corpus (window 2,048, bf16). Changed slots of 50, mean over all poles: base allenai/Olmo-3-1025-7B -> Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math step 2,800 (main): 2.11 (by 8-layer band 1.14, 2.34, 2.36, 2.61; layer 0 0.83 rising to layer 31 3.05). Base -> step_0100: 0.98. Step 100 -> 2,800: 2.09. Yardsticks from banked harvests, computed before the RL pairs: same checkpoint on two instances 0.00; same checkpoint in two grid runs 0.84 (noise floor); adjacent pretraining stage-1 checkpoints 30.2-38.3; stage-1 start -> a 100B-token stage-2 mix 29.8-32.5; t00 -> t15 50.0. Frozen label: AT PRETRAINING-NEIGHBOUR LEVEL in every band (the RL change is 11-27x smaller per band than the closest pair of pretraining checkpoints, t14 -> t15, and about 2.5x the noise floor; step 100 is at the noise floor). Limit: a top-50 set ignores any monotone rescaling and any change that shows only on math text (RLN-2 measures those). Status: closed, frozen spec, not audited by a second reader. Artifacts: interp_research-clean-neurons/studies/rlneurons/results/rl_pairs.json, yardsticks.json, SPEC.md (commit 66ab107b8).

From interp_research rlneurons (RLN-2): the base and RL models compute almost the same MLP activations on general text and diverge on math solutions, more with depth. Both models run on the same tokens (bf16, activation = input of mlp.down_proj, per-neuron Pearson r between base and RL over tokens). From interp_research rlneurons (RLN-4 loop detectors): use the zlib rule (rule A), not a period rule or a repeated-line count, to call base-model loops. Rule A: an 8,000-character window starting at a line start with zlib compression ratio < 0.10; onset = first line of the repeated block. Tested on saved MATH-500 answers (T 0.6, cap 16,384): fires on 0 of 484 RL finished answers, 1 of 431 base plain (n13), 0 of 435 and 0 of 381 for two base-01 cells; fires on 59 of 60, 46 of 48 and 90 of 92 low-ratio cap hits. Rule B (period <= 64 characters over >= 2,000 characters, 3 cycles; as relayed from arXiv 2611.06095, paper not read) has no false positives but catches only 6-17 % of the loops, because the base's loops have periods of hundreds of characters. A crude rule (any line > 20 characters three times) fires on 60 of 484 RL finished answers, so it fails. Caveat: on low-ratio cap hits rule A's hit rate is nearly guaranteed by construction; the test is the false-positive side, and the onset was checked by eye on 4 answers only. At T 1.0 rule A finds 0 loops in T1, T2 and T3 (500 each); the cued base at T 0.6 has 92 low-ratio cap hits of 119. Status: closed instrument check, not audited. Artifacts: interp_research-clean-neurons/studies/rlneurons/rln4/offline/prep_checks.json (detector), SPEC4.md section 4; code iterate-hack studies/rlneurons/lib/rln4_lib.py onset_lines.

From interp_research rlneurons (RLN-4 grader v3 limits): two known ways grader v3 errs, and the format split behind most v1 misses. (1) A mid-line 'Answer:' marker also matches when the model invents and answers a new problem after its real answer; that is the only right-to-wrong flip of 114 over 9 cells (plain base T 1.0, problem 146: v1 right, v3 takes 'Answer: $60$' of an invented COFFEE problem). (2) A tail of three or more letters glued to a number is cut even when it is a product of variables ('2xyz' becomes '2'). v3 checks: 500/500 golds equal themselves, 3 equal after a derangement, planted pairs 24/24 and 16/16, 22 audited rows. Why v1 failed: the base ends with an 'Answer:' line in 39-46 % of answers and RL boxes (n13: 'Answer:' line share base 0.44, RL 0.00); v1/v2 found no answer in 166 of 500 plain-base T 1.0 answers and 127 of 500 plain-base T 0.6 answers. This format difference is also what drives the RLN-5 log-prob gap at the answer start (result-fdc8da). The v1 -> v3 flip counts are already on the board (knowledge-781efc). Status: closed, one reader; no second model has read the v3 rescoring (open). (1) Of the 100 MLP neurons whose copy from RL moves the base most (Part T2), 44 are on almost everywhere (|a| beyond the layer p97 at > 50 % of 131,397 positions) vs 1 of 100 layer-matched random neurons; median mean |a| 0.213 vs 0.020; their gate/up/down weights have cosine 1.0000 with RL's. Accuracy: 90.7 % [86.0, 94.7] for 30 of the best neurons, 71.3 % [60.0, 81.3] for 15 random neurons, chance 50 %. So single neurons of this 7B model are describable at their peaks. nodes.text: Literature from interp_research, 30 papers read in full, 147 findings in past.dev (recall.py). What bears on the direction: (1) RL gain is sparse in tokens and re-weights base behavior: swapping the RL token at 4-8% of positions lifts base AIME24 to RL level, RL token is in base top-3 >80% (2603.22446); RL keeps the base's forking positions, 86.7% overlap (2506.01939); base Olmo-3-7B already writes 'wait' ~5/1k, RL-Zero-Math 76.5/1k at T 0.6 with 29.1% length-limit hits vs 17.8% base (2610.30882); URIAL: 92% of chat tokens in base top-3, shift at the start (2312.01552). Spurious rewards help only where the behavior exists; OLMo2 flat (2506.10947). (2) Weight difference: rank-1 of the RL update, rescaled, keeps ~100% of MATH-500 gain, lambda peak ~0.7 (2510.00553); update x0.75 +3.4 GSM8K, matched-norm random update 59.5->5% (2610.22438); Olmo-3 RL-Zero leverage 708x random, carried by signs; x1.5 breaks stopping (stop rate to 0.005-0.18) (2610.37719); top 0.1% Fisher mask gives 85% of RL gain vs random 23.9 (2609.36262); RL update is rotation not rescaling, incl. OLMo-3 Think-RL (2609.22146); DARE needs deltas <=~0.002, fails >0.01 (2311.03099); Bolmo moves an Olmo-3 RL-Zero IF delta to a byte model, IFEval 31.1->67.4 (2512.15586); 13 params give 74.6 vs 78.2 full on MATH-500 (2602.04118). Fine-tune sparsity is bf16 rounding, gone in fp32 (2509.04259). (3) Loops: loop onset = entropy drops to ~0 after a Wait/But burst, probe flags 64-76% ~1,500 tokens early (2601.05693); Olmo-3-7B-Think cap hits only 62% loops (2611.06095); loop-neuron edits beat random in 4/8 cells and can turn loops into endless reasoning (2606.13705); repetition-neuron ablation fixes ~30% (2410.13497). (4) Decode-time/steering: SEAL keyword-labeled vector, R1-Distill-7B MATH-500 85.8->89.4 with -21% tokens (2504.07986); proxy-tuning on first tokens only fails (base falls back to repetition) (2401.08565); forced Wait barely moves MATH500 (2501.19393); SAE steering recovers format, not reasoning (2609.15064). Plus 25 board items of interp_research's own results (knowledge-9c5052...). work-02efb7

nodes.text: RL gain as context: does a context window carry what the RL weight difference carries? Base + cue, MATH-500, T 1.0/top-p 1.0, grader v3, n 500, same run_cell harness with a longer prefix. Prefix = 3 solved problems from MATH train (none in MATH-500 or the 328), each about 1,500 tokens, in the test template, then the test problem and the cue. Arms differ only in who wrote the 3 answers: (i) cued base, picked without an answer key (4 samples agree, finished), (ii) Math-RL 3.1, (iii) Code-RL 3.1, (iv) control: cued base answers picked at random, same token count. Baselines: base cue 410, theta(0.25) cue 441, RL cue 457. Arm (v), only if (ii) < 441: 16 trainable prefix vectors fit by KL to RL's next-token distribution on RL's MATH-train answers (no reward), as the upper bound of any context. Why: a=0.25 plain (405) equals the cue (410), both RL deltas read out the cue token (result-e2482e), Code-RL gives the math gain with cos 0.014 (result-4b0d5f), and 2505.14216 Table 1 finds SFT on RL's answers gives +11.6 pts while SFT on the base's own correct answers gives +0.8: the gain is in how RL writes, not in correctness. Not tested in context on a base model (Wang 2610.06851 tests only RL's opening of the same problem, 77.7 = cue). Readings: (i) >= 430 is a label-free route with no RL model at all; (ii) >= 441 with (i),(iv) <= 420 means 3 pasted RL answers carry the gain, then run the same 3 answers on a base model of another family that has no RL release; all arms <= 420 and (v) < 441 refutes: context cannot carry it. Generated tokens are equal by design; prompt tokens are reported. Cost: 4 cells, forward only, about 4 USD. Choose on MATH-500, score the best arm once on the 328.

nodes.text: Reward content test: does the MATH-500 gain need a math reward, a reasoning reward, or only RL from the base? AI2 released RL-Zero models from the same base for 5 rewards (names read from HF 02:18 UTC): Olmo-3-7B-RL-Zero-IF, -General, -Mix, -Code, -Math, plus 3.1 Code and Math. We have 2 points: Code-RL cue 450 vs Math-RL cue 457 of 500, weight differences cos 0.014 (result-4b0d5f). Step 1, about 5 cells, 9 USD: IF, General, Mix (and 3.0 Math, Code as same-version controls), cue and plain, MATH-500, T 1.0/top-p 1.0, v3, same run_cell. Baselines: base cue 410, random difference 417, theta(0.25) 441, RL 457. Step 2, forward only: teacher-force base, each RL model, the random difference and theta(0.25) on the same 2,000 stored base answers (job 208b); per token r_m = log p_m - log p_base. Measure the correlation of r across models over positions, and at the 10 percent of positions with the largest |r_Math| whether the other models prefer the same token (2603.22117: replacing those 10 percent of tokens gives the full RL score). Null: the random difference, and Math 3.0 vs 3.1 as the ceiling. Readings: IF cue >= 441 and r_IF agrees with r_Math far above the random null means the gain is the same set of token decisions whatever the reward, so it is a property of the base model, and the next step is to predict those positions from the base alone (label-free). IF cue <= 420 with Code at 450 means the reward must grade a reasoning task. Equal scores with r uncorrelated means different decisions reach the same score. Not published: 2608.03573 reports orthogonal RL updates across tasks and no harm to other tasks, 2509.01363 Sec 4.4 a +2 pt cross-task gain with no control, 2610.24663 and 2603.22117 use one RL model each; none compares token decisions across rewards. Check each model's base and tensor layout on its card before any merge.

nodes.text: cleanneurons Part T3 (is the RL change a constant push?), Olmo 3 base vs RL-Zero-Math, held-out 2,672 decisive positions after the cue (T1 text / T2 text): adding ONE constant vector per layer to the base (mean of RL-layer minus base-layer output, 32 vectors, no weight change) closes 23.4 / 31.2 % of KL(RL||base); a random vector of the same norm: -1.6 / -4.7 %. A constant on the MLP output only: 14.0 / 15.1 %, i.e. 17-21 % of what all MLP weights close (67.7 / 86.4 %), so 'the MLP change is mostly a constant vector' is refuted. The 472 always-on neurons (0.13 % of 352,256; 110 in the last layer) copied from RL close 2.6 / 3.4 %, vs 0.1-0.2 % for 472 other neurons. Picture: RL = a fixed, direction-specific push per layer (about a quarter to a third) + small input-dependent changes over almost every neuron. Controls passed. Limit: teacher-forced distance to RL, not accuracy. Job sameraslan-1114-184552-a899 (H100, 6 min), commit a2ec2c9. Artifact: branch claude/clean-neuron-hypothesis-9e2ed3, studies/cleanneurons/results/transplant/curve_bias-01/metrics.json, README.md. work-383069.

plain.title: One fixed vector per layer closes a quarter of RL's shift
plain.what: Adding one constant vector per layer to the base (32 vectors, no weight change) closed 23 to 31 % of the gap between base and RL next-token predictions. A random vector of the same size closed none.
plain.why: The RL change looks like a fixed push per layer plus small input-dependent changes spread over almost every neuron; the MLP change is mostly not a constant.
plain.caveat: Measures closeness to RL's next-token predictions on fixed text rather than accuracy on problems.

nodes.text:
Literature sweep 2026-11-15 (work-6b1fa5): 11 pieces read in full by subagents, 45 findings sent to past.dev (tools/paper.py add); texts in papers/<id>.txt. Safety/alignment work excluded. Exa was down (EXA_API_KEY unset), search was plain web. Ranked for the base-vs-RL gap:
1. arxiv-2611.09382 'Exploring Weight-Space Programming' (Shanghai AI Lab, 11-06; NOT an MIT follow-up, an independent replication; code github.com/WSP-Scope/WSP-Scope-Project). One-column edit on Qwen3.5-0.8B: u = normalised (mean embedding of Wait/However/But/Maybe/Perhaps minus mean of Therefore/Thus/So/Now/The/First/Next/Let), layers.23.mlp.down_proj[:,507] -= u. MATH-500 8.35 -> 37.80; on Qwen3.5-9B 97.70 -> 97.35 (no gain where the model does not loop). Controls on 48 questions: base 6, edit 20, column ablation 4, reversed 0, equal-norm random direction 10. Three searches gave +29.45, +5.00, +27.30 points. Proposed: same u from Olmo readout rows, subtracted from the late down_proj columns where the RL delta projects most on u, a in {0.5, 1}, both signs. Refuted if cap hits fall no more than with an equal-norm random direction.
2. arxiv-2608.17124 CASE (08-17): logistic probe on the answer-token residual picks 1 of 4 samples. Qwen2.5-7B MATH-500: within-question AUC 0.763, +2.6 points over vote on hard questions (p<0.001). Needs labels on about 50 calibration questions; a naive probe is at chance within a question (0.502). Proposed: fit on base samples from 100 non-MATH-500 problems, select among our stored 4. Refuted if within-question AUC < 0.60 or it does not beat tie_short 453/500 (pass@4 is 467).
3. arxiv-2607.19331 ISO (07-21): the RL update is rotation of singular vectors, not a change of singular values; remixing inside base subspaces leaves a median 87 % of the update unexplained. Task arithmetic of two RL experts: AIME24 50.83. Proposed: U_RL S_base V_RL^T for Olmo on MATH-500. Refuted if it falls more than 2 points below RL.
4. Goodfire 'Neural Networks Are Already Clean' (10-15, web-785656d81e): neuron-level clamps change looping (zeroing outputs above the 99.9th gate percentile makes Qwen3.6-35B repeat a phrase to the cap). No code. Proposed: set the 50 late-MLP neurons with the largest RL-minus-base change to RL levels in base. Refuted if loop rate moves no more than with 50 random same-layer neurons.
5. 'Sparks of Weight-Space Programming' (web-32b3bf2b22) is the full title of the blog in knowledge-c9fc18; no separate paper. The gain is cap hits only (93.0 -> 33.1 %), so the share of base+cue errors that are cap hits is the ceiling for any loop edit: count it first. The formula W <- W - 6u(u^T W) in knowledge-c1fe13 is not in the blog text.
Lower: arxiv-2509.01363 Reasoning Vectors (GRPO-minus-SFT vector, Qwen2.5-7B GSM8K 55.3 -> 58.9, cue adds on top: 60.3; agrees with our theta result). arxiv-2608.19611 Forking Fast (Goodfire; locates the token where an outcome becomes fixed, code released; use on loop onsets). arxiv-2605.26172 ARBITER (MATH-500 Qwen3-4B vote 69.20, top-2 oracle 76.60; hidden-state rerank and self-review fragile, agrees with result-96e819). arxiv-2607.18100 SOPHIA (loop-exit steering vector, no accuracy reported). Goodfire parameter decomposition (web-4043a8cbfa): 67M-parameter model only, 400,000 steps, not usable at 7B. Goodfire Manifold Steering arxiv-2605.05115: no accuracy evidence.
Not verified: Olmo MLP activation type (decides whether Goodfire's SwiGLU findings apply); no repo opened.

nodes.text:
PICK for the next interpretability study (work-3946b0: 4 proposers, 12 proposals, inventory of our own studies, 2 skeptics; both skeptics rank it first): WHAT RL WRITES REGARDLESS OF REWARD.
Claim: RL runs with different rewards (Math, Code, IF, General, Mix, all from allenai/Olmo-3-1025-7B, verified on HF) write the same few singular directions per matrix, and those directions taken only from runs that never saw a math reward give the base the math-RL gain. Refuted if top-8 subspace overlap between rewards is within 3 sd of the random rank-8 null, or the non-math edit scores no better than matched random on hard328 with cue.
Step 1 (weights only, <1 h, ~60 new lines on wsp_delta_anatomy.py, branch claude/weight-space-programming-research-ddd44e): per matrix, mean squared principal cosine between top-8 singular subspaces of each pair of deltas. Start with Math 3.1 vs Code 3.1 (cached). Nulls: random rank-8, Think-SFT delta. Ceiling: Math 3.0 vs Math 3.1. Picture: 7x7 heat map beside its null.
Step 2 (edits, ~80 new lines: a projection recipe in wsp_edit.py with a planted self-test): base + top-8 of IF; + top-8 of General; + Math delta projected on the non-math shared span; + Math top-8 with that span removed; + matched random rank-8; + Think-SFT top-8. First cell ~2 h.
Step 3 (weights only): the same overlap at steps 100/200/400/800 per reward, against a within-reward split-half ceiling: do rewards share an early phase?
Mandatory controls (from our own results): score with the cue on hard328 (base 164, RL 206 of 328; a paired comparison resolves ~5 points), never on plain MATH-500 alone, because Think-SFT with a delta orthogonal to RL scores 91/100 plain and a random delta also gains; same-release pairs (Code 3.0 + cue 411 vs Code 3.1 450); report the effective scale after bf16 rounding (54 % of delta entries are within one ulp); 4 samples per arm where arms differ by under 5 points.
Why novel: published work has whole-update cosines between RL runs (2609.22146: 0.003-0.037), Fisher leverage on the same Olmo deltas (2610.37719), and one-run compact cores (SAR 2607.03065, abstract only). None transfers a subspace from one reward as an edit that gives another reward's gain. Novelty checked from team memory and abstracts, no paper read in full for this.

nodes.text: Subagents started inside the repository see result numbers that the prompt never gave them: Claude Code puts the 5 newest commit subjects (git status block) into every subagent's context, and our commit subjects carry scores (e.g. 'Day-1 #3 MATH-500 results: base+cue single 405, restart 413, vote4 446 ...'). Found in theory round 02, where a generator reported it; two agents copied their 5 lines on request (studies/theory/results/engine/round-02/exposed.json). Any blind test run through the Agent tool is affected: blind judges, held-out prediction, planted-case reviews. Fix that worked: run the blind call headless from an empty directory outside the repo, 'claude -p --restricted --strict-mcp-config --tools Read,Write --allowedTools Read Write < prompt.txt', with only its input files copied in; its context then has no git status, no CLAUDE.md, no MCP tools (tested; studies/theory/lib/round.py does this for every blind stage). Plain '--allowedTools Read Write' alone does not restrict the tools.

RL-Zero without the reward (plan, not started; riskier follow-up to idea-607778). Thesis: one RL sample is the base's own 4-sample vote paid once in weights. Evidence: RL single 456 vs base vote 446-453 and pass@4 467 (result-5d032f, cbe0bc); the vote adds 8.2 pts to base but 3.6 to RL; the RL delta is 0.24% of weight norm and 8 directions per matrix carry most of it (result-ad3c24). So the reward may be replaceable by agreement among the base's own samples, with truncated answers as negatives (3.0 -> 3.1 added exactly that, and only Code 3.1 transfers to math: 450 vs Code 3.0 411, result-edceef). Stage 0, stored rows, no GPU: among problems where no base sample of 4 is right, how often is RL right; and when the base plurality is wrong, how often RL gives the same wrong answer. Thesis refuted if RL is right on more than half of the pass@4 failures. Stage 1, one GPU job: gradient of log-prob of the stored base samples with sign +1 for plurality-agreeing finished samples and -1 for minority and cap-hit samples; no answer key. Measure its top-8 subspace overlap and cosine with the RL-Math delta against a random null and against the same gradient built with the true key (ceiling). Stage 2: base + one step of that gradient at the norm of 0.25 (RL - base); cue, hard328, vs base 164, theta0.25 182, RL 206. Controls: matched-norm random (417-level null), sign flipped, positives only, true-key. Stage 3 only if stage 2 gains >= 3 pts: on-policy loop on unlabeled MATH-train problems, 4 samples, agreement as reward, rank-8 LoRA, 50-100 steps; first score RL-Zero step_050/100/200 with the cue to see how many steps RL itself needed. Known against it: 2509.04259 (on-policy data matters, not negatives), 2607.13643 and 2505.14216 (SFT on own agreeing or correct answers gives < 1 pt), a wrong plurality gets reinforced. Published neighbour: TTRL uses vote as an online reward; not done from a base model beside a released RL-Zero delta, and no one-step alignment test.

comments.text: Stage 0 done on stored rows (day1_3, 4 samples x 500): thesis not refuted. RL right on 28% of samples where base is 0/4 (33 problems). Of RL's +49.5 expected problems, 9.2 come from base 0/4, 11.2 from 1/4, 9.2 from 2/4, 21.5 from 3/4: agreement can supply about 45-60%.

Stages 1-2 run: refuted offline. Signed update with vote (140/328) or key (155) as return is below base cue 164; the model doubts more and hits the cap. result of work-d9a824. Open: online resampling, per-step instead of per-sample credit.

nodes.text: Policy improvement at decoding time, no weights and no reward (plan, not started; riskier follow-up to idea-46b68c). Thesis: what is left of the RL gain is reliability, not knowledge: any of 4 base samples is right on 467/500 (MATH-500) and 205/328 (hard328, = RL single 206), and RL stores in weights the choice a critic could make while decoding. Replace the weights by a critic read from the base's own activations, trained with no answer key (target: will this sample agree with the plurality of 4), and use it to stop a failing sample early and start again. Differs from idea-0d55a4 (vote as a reward for weight updates) and from the length rules (result-2c2cae: +0.9 to +3.7 pts at up to 2.2x tokens): no weight changes, and the critic acts before the length is known. Stage 0, stored rows, no GPU: accuracy and tokens of stop-and-restart with a perfect critic at 10/25/50 % of the answer; stop if it cannot reach 440/500 at <= 1.5x tokens. Stage 1, one forward job: probe on base residual activations at 10/25/50 % of the 2,000 stored MATH-500 samples, 5 folds by problem, AUROC for plurality agreement and (evaluation only) correctness, vs tokens so far, mean log-prob and entropy so far. Stop if AUROC at 25 % is within 0.03 of the best of those. Stage 2: threshold chosen on MATH-500, scored once on hard328 for base and RL with tokens per problem; target base >= 190/328 at <= 1.3x tokens (theta(0.5) 190, RL 206). Stage 3 only if stage 2 gains: at the 10 % highest-entropy positions score the top tokens with the critic and compare the choices with the tokens Math-RL prefers (score_tokens instrument, result-edceef step 2). Against it: result-f21d2e (no J-lens feature beats length for a wrong base answer, AUROC 0.831), 2608.17124 and 2605.09502 (the correctness direction is a readout, steering with it does not help), 2504.05419 (probes for own correctness exist, on trained reasoning models). Checked today on 500 stored base answers: the summed log-ratio log p_RL - log p_base separates right from wrong at AUROC 0.853, the same as length alone (0.855), and the per-token mean does not favour right answers, so the RL model's likelihood is not a usable critic.

nodes.text: RL's gain on MATH-500 is mostly a reliability shift: 81% of the 198-sample gap (4 samples per problem, n=500, T 1.0, v3; base+cue 1,642 right of 2,000, RL 1,840) sits in problems the base solves at least once in 4; 19% [11, 27] in problems with base 0 of 4. Cell base 3/4 -> RL 4/4: 86 problems = 43% of the gap. Held-out check (class by 3 base samples, score the 4th): the class 'other three wrong' holds 14% [5, 23] of the gap and the base still solves 15% there; in the class 'other three right' the base fails 7.2%, RL 0.9% (43% of the gap). Homogeneous binomial null predicts 0.5 problems at 0/4, observed 33. Only 2 problems go from 0/4 to 4/4 (170, 279); of the 33 base-0/4 problems RL has 0/4 on 16. Level 5 holds 44% [35, 54] of the gap (27% of problems); Intermediate Algebra 30% [22, 39] (19%). Base wrong samples: 250 finished-wrong, 89 cap hits, 19 no answer; RL is right on the same problems 68%, 49%, 83%. Blind judge (Claude subagents with a fixed rubric; no hosted provider key works on this machine) on 60 base / 30 RL finished-wrong: base slip 35% [24, 48], wrong plan 28%, misread 23%, format 13%; RL slip 17%, wrong plan 67%, misread 17%, format 0. Two passes agree on 44 of 45, kappa 0.97 (same model). Controls: shuffled pairs 15/15 mismatch; planted slips 11/15 and 13/15 (misses all labeled format: slip vs format is unreliable for an error in the last line). Base items with a right sibling: 39 of 48 slip/misread/format; without (base 0/4): 8 of 12 wrong plan. About 52 of the base's 358 wrong samples (36 to 79) fail in stating the answer (placeholder left, form rejected by v3, no answer); RL 0. First wrong step at median 0.20 of the answer. plain.title: Using each day's highest GPU price improves the forecast

nodes.text: Where does low temperature help and where does it loop? (for hard328; config chosen on MATH-500). Facts: cued base at T 0.6 is more accurate when it finishes (378 vs ~362 at T 1.0 on the same 402 MATH-500 problems, knowledge-13cff3) but loops on 98/500; min-p 0.1 at T 1.0 also raises finished accuracy (404/442 vs 410/473) and brings loops back (result-44b4df). Both sharpen every position. Test: a per-token rule in a vLLM logits processor, logits/T_low only where next-token entropy H is above h0 (the top 20 % of positions, 'forking tokens' of 2506.01939), T 1.0 elsewhere; 2x2 with the reverse gate, constant T_low and T 1.0, T_low in {0.6, 0.3}. Hypothesis: loops come from sharpening confident positions (the tail tokens there are the exits from a repeated block), accuracy from sharpening forks. Refuted if the forks-only arm has cap hits at the T 0.6 level, or no more right than T 1.0. Either outcome says which positions carry the T 0.6 gain. Then the winner once on the 328, both models. Not the loop-triggered temperature boost (llama.cpp PR 22007): no loop detector, the gate is the entropy alone.

nodes.text: RL does not win by checking more: it writes more checking markers (13.1 vs 9.5 per 1k tokens, paired +3.6 [3.4, 3.9], n=500, all of it wait/hmm/actually), but markers do not separate right from wrong samples of the same model and problem (base right minus wrong +0.63 [-0.01, 1.28] per 1k, +0.08 [-0.64, 0.77] at matched length, 150 problems; RL wrong samples have more), the rate after 52 located base wrong steps equals that of right siblings (9.2 vs 9.2; a marker within 500 tokens after 88 % of steps vs 87 % at random positions), and blind judges call 5 of 80 check events a fix (base 3 of 40, RL 2 of 40; kappa 0.88, planted controls 20 of 20 and 19 of 20). 6 of 11 base slips read are followed by a check that repeats the slip. What differs: first wrong steps per 1k finished tokens, 0.015 RL vs 0.038 base. Not separable at 40 events per model: fewer errors made vs a larger share caught. Judges are the agent's own subagents. Prediction filed on work-74703c: Wait steering changes the cued base by 0 points [-2, +1]. studies/rlneurons/results/checks/math500-01/ and judge-01/, README section 'Checks or per-step error', commit adafdc5.

plain.title: RL does not win by checking its work more
plain.what: RL writes more checking words such as 'wait' and 'hmm' (13.1 vs 9.5 per 1,000 tokens), but these words do not separate right from wrong answers, and judges called only 5 of 80 checks a real fix.
plain.why: RL makes fewer first wrong steps (0.015 vs 0.038 per 1,000 tokens). Whether it makes fewer errors or catches more of them could not be told apart.
plain.caveat: The judges were the agent's own subagents, and only 40 check events per model were read.

nodes.text: Activation edits during generation run inside vLLM 0.32 at vLLM speed, no Hugging Face generate needed. vLLM serves Olmo 3 through its Transformers backend, so model.model.layers[l] are the Hugging Face blocks and a torch forward hook on a block acts on every sequence of the batch (hidden state [1, tokens of all running requests, 4096]). Needed: VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING=0 (model in the job's process), EngineArgs(enforce_eager=True) (a Python hook is not replayed by a CUDA graph), enable_prefix_caching=False when arms differ in activations; find the model by walking the engine's attributes (vLLM freezes the gc list). Per-request logit_bias works with seeded sampling. Instrument check to copy: a huge edit must change every answer (alpha 8 gave only 'wait' tokens). Measured: 17 arms x 63 problems x 1,024 tokens in 11 minutes on one H100; a 500-problem arm at cap 16,384 in 31 to 35 minutes, the same as run_cell; a random direction of 6.8 % of the block norm scores 409/500 (stored unsteered cells 404 to 418). Within-problem AUROC (good vs bad sample of the same problem, 110-137 problems): 0.51 / 0.54 / 0.571 [0.509, 0.634] / 0.51; the same probe trained on the answer key 0.51-0.55; mean log-prob and entropy so far 0.49-0.57. Across problems the probe at the last prompt token predicts the flag at 0.73-0.77: the base encodes how hard the problem is before writing, not which sample goes wrong. Offline stop-and-restart at 1,000 tokens with the probe: 414.1/500 at 4,345 tokens vs one sample 410.5 at 4,008; probe minus random-score +0.8 pts [-0.7, 2.4]. Ceiling with a perfect critic at 1,000 tokens: 438.7 (no key) and 459.2 (key) at about 4,100 tokens, RL single 456. C1-C3 refuted. Checks: exactly 0.500 at the prompt position, 0.49-0.50 with flags shuffled within problems, planted signal found. Limits: linear, one position, 3 layers, n 2,000; a critic that reads the finished answer was not tested. Note for anyone voting on stored rows: comparing extracted_v3 strings splits equal answers (39 % of problems look unanimous); group with rln4_lib.agree. plain.title: Base activations cannot tell which sample will fail
plain.what: A linear probe on the cued base's internal activations tried to tell good from bad samples of the same problem. Over 2,000 MATH-500 samples it scored an AUROC of 0.51 to 0.57, close to chance (0.5).
plain.why: Before writing, the probe predicts how hard a problem is (AUROC 0.73 to 0.77): the activations encode difficulty rather than which sample goes wrong.
plain.caveat: Only linear probes at 3 layers and one position were tested, on 2,000 samples; a critic that reads the finished answer was not tested.

plain.title: RL does not cut errors by one fixed factor

plain.why: RL's error ratio against the base depends on difficulty: 0.48 on the 46 hardest problems, 0.23 on the middle 119, 0.11 on the 335 easiest.
plain.caveat: The reading of which side of the logistic model the data lie on was made after the fact, and hazard predictions for 5 running cells were not yet scored.

nodes.text: Math-RL is about half as likely as the base to write the base's own located wrong step, and the base's wrong step is not an unlikely sample. 51 judged finished-wrong samples of the cued base (MATH-500; first wrong step located, median 29 tokens), D = (log p_model - log p_base) over the step minus the same over 200 control spans of the same answer, nats [95 %]: Mix 3.0 -0.80 [-1.34, -0.28], Math 3.1 -0.71 [-1.48, 0.01] (factor 0.49; measured ratio of first wrong steps 0.39, result-855858), Math 3.0 -0.58, Code 3.1 -0.45 [-0.79, -0.12], Code 3.0 -0.32 [-0.95, 0.27], General -0.14, theta(0.25) -0.10, random difference 0.00 [-0.02, 0.02], IF +0.17. Order follows the cue gain of result-edceef (Spearman -0.67, n 9). By label for Math 3.1: misread -1.52, slip -0.72, wrong plan +0.03: RL lowers misreadings and slips, not wrong plans. Under the base the wrong step has log-prob -0.53 per token vs -0.63 for control text (W4 refuted): truncation or low temperature cannot remove these steps, which fits the min-p/top-p negatives. W1 not met as written (interval touches 0; the effect is in a minority of items, median -0.26), W2, W3 held. Limits: 51 items, judges are our subagents. Artifacts: studies/rlneurons/results/wrongstep/math500-01/{metrics,items}.json, README section 'Wrong steps', branch critic. About 3 USD.

plain.title: Math RL is half as likely to write the base's wrong step
plain.what: In 51 wrong answers of the cued base, the first wrong step was located. Math RL 3.1 gives that step about half the base's probability (factor 0.49), relative to other text of the answer; a random weight change gives no shift.
plain.why: RL lowers misreadings and slips and leaves wrong plans unchanged. The base finds these steps fairly likely, so sampling settings that cut rare tokens cannot remove them.
plain.caveat: Only 51 items, judged by our own agents, and the Math 3.1 interval touches zero.

The theory: part of the cued base's accuracy is recall from pretraining, so at matched difficulty the RL gap is larger on problems published after the base's cutoff. It survived its own tests on +0.12 nats (post-cutoff excess +6.9 points on 60 problems at T 1.0). The cued base's T 0.6 loops feed on its own text: loop hazard grows with how compressible (zlib) the text so far is. Own tests: +1.41 nats on 3 of 4. For it: within a problem the capped sample's opening compresses better than a finishing restart's in 37 of 46 (theory 0.63, rival 0.53). Against it: where RL's opening is as compressible as the base's, RL's prefix still helps by 0.375 (24 problems; theory 0.12 [-0.07, 0.31]); a more compressible opening does not bring the loop earlier (rank correlation -0.074, 62 loops; theory 0.2). So compressibility marks the sample that will loop but does not explain RL's prefix advantage. Nearest: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.05693. Negative: giving the cued base the RL model's Wait habit does not raise MATH-500 (SPEC3, idea-da9dca, work-74703c). The J-lens direction of Wait/Hmm added to layer 24 during generation until the base writes them at the RL model's rate (8.32 per 1,000 tokens; RL 8.81; unsteered 6.28): 413/500, n=500, T 1.0, cap 16,384, v3. Against four stored unsteered samples (mean 410.5): +0.5 pts [-2.2, +3.1]; against a random direction of the same norm (409): +0.8 [-2.6, +4.2]; RL is 457. Stronger push (alpha 0.1, 11.2 per 1,000): 381, -5.9 [-9.0, -2.9]; 39 answers end without an answer (unsteered 5). Same written rate from layer 20: 398. Logit bias on the six tokens (0.64 nats, 9.72 per 1,000): 421, not below the push (push minus bias -1.6 [-5.0, +1.8]), so the workspace adds nothing over a decoding bias. Why: (1) the push adds the word without a check: a blind reader labelled 16 of 20 push-inserted Waits as filler, 1 as a fix; of the model's own Waits 7 of 20 are fixes; (2) on the 65 problems T1 missed and T2 solved: unsteered 42, random 35, push 35; (3) inside, the push overshoots: hold-on words in the layer-24 readout at 31 % of positions, vs 4.75 % unsteered and 6.29 % in RL; alpha 0.017 already gives 7.2 %. The readout difference is a trace of the habit, not its cause. nodes.text: xreward trace (forward pass, base model on its own 328 hard328 answers, 1,572,055 positions, job abaybektursun-1115-005830-2145): the base's MLP inputs drive the 8 input directions of the Math 3.1 difference 8.1 to 11.2 times more than a random subspace with the same singular values (by layer band); Code 3.1's 6.3 to 8.9 times; IF's 2.0 to 4.5 times. So the top-8 input subspaces sit on directions that math-solution text really excites, more for the reasoning rewards than for IF: support for reading the input-side overlap of result-9d979a as a trace of the text a run generated. The edit changes each matrix's output by under 0.6 %. Nulls: drive does not differ between cap-hit and finished answers (ratio 0.99 to 1.01); at Wait/Hmm/perhaps positions it is 1.22x other positions but So/Therefore/Then is 1.17x, so the check-specific excess is 5 to 10 %, and Code 3.1 shows the same. No cap hit has a loop onset by rule A or B at T 1.0. Caveat: bootstrap intervals pool positions and are too narrow. Artifacts studies/rlneurons/results/xreward/trace-01/readout.json, spec specs/SPEC_xreward_trace.md, branch sharedsub.

comments.text: Numbers reproduce (Math 8.1-11.2x random). But 9-17x at layers 29-31 holds for Math, Code and IF alike: a delta's input directions lie in its training-input span, so any fine-tune may beat an isotropic null. Controls needed: Think-SFT delta, top-8 input PCs, non-math text.

plain.title: Math text strongly excites RL's 8 key weight directions
plain.what: Fed its own answers to 328 harder problems, the base's internal inputs push on the top 8 directions of math RL's weight change 8 to 11 times more than on random ones; 6 to 9 times for code RL, 2 to 4.5 for instruction-following RL.
plain.why: The team reads this as the directions reflecting the text each RL run generated, which fits the math and code rewards more than instruction following.
plain.caveat: The push is the same in answers that hit the length cap and in finished ones, and only 5 to 10 % higher at check words like Wait; the confidence intervals are too narrow.

title: Budget of the cued-base-to-RL gap in four cells: loops replace reliability at T 0.6
what: Fixed rules sort each problem the RL model solves and the cued base misses into loop, budget (cap hit), answer statement, reliability (base right in another stored row) or capability.
why: It shows where the gap sits; at T 1.0 a fresh base sample's gap has RL's budget.
caveat: Gross gaps, one sample per side; hard328 evidence rows weaker (T 0.6, v1); T 0.6 cell graded v1.
Shares (n; loop/budget/answer/reliability/capability; 3 evidence rows): MATH-500 T 1.0 RL 65: 0/.25/.03/.63/.09; theta0.5 53: 0/.21/.04/.64/.11; hard328 Code-RL 37: 0/.27/.03/.43/.27; step 400 T 0.6 66: .44/.12/.06/.38/0; base resample 42: 0/.17/.02/.67/.14. Apart at 90 %: only T 0.6 loop, reliability, capability against each MATH-500 T 1.0 cell, and hard328 capability against RL. Surprise: T 0.6 reliability .38, predicted .15; 9 of its 25 are right answers v1 rejects. studies/theory/results/account/run-02/readout.md (branch theory, a92ae63 and later)

comments.text: Reproduced. Regraded v3 the T 0.6 cell gives gap 56, loops .54, reliability .30: the claim gets stronger. That cell also differs in RL checkpoint (step 400), top-p 0.95 and base row (340, not 378); a final-RL T 0.6 cell would isolate temperature.

Account run 03 confirms (51 of 51 shares recomputed equal): at MATH-500 T 1.0 no part of RL's or Code-RL's gap differs from a base-resample null. Correction: reliability is 0.43-0.48 with 2 evidence rows, 0.63-0.67 with 3. studies/theory/results/account/run-03/readout.md

nodes.text: Theory round 05 rival (replaces r5-m03 'top-8 directions = the cue and nothing more'): the top-8 edit of the RL-Math weight change is an incomplete switch per sample. About 85-90 % of base+top8 plain answers follow a weak dose of RL's policy (longer, checking, few quick wrong answers); the other 10-15 % stay in the plain-base register (short, wrong about half the time at any difficulty). Duel on stored MATH-500 rows, 3 of 3 tests favour it, total 8.77 nats against r5-m03: share of top8's wrong problems that the cued base solves 4 of 4: 0.25 (rival 0.27, theory 0.13); mean cued-base solve rate on top8's quick finished-wrong answers: 0.818 (rival 0.76, theory 0.5); share of those with at most 1,000 tokens: 0.773 (rival 0.63, theory 0.4). One rival, 3 tests, not recomputed independently. GPU test, not run (45 min H100): base+top8 WITH the cue on MATH-500; r5-m03 says 425 [412, 438] of 500 (cue redundant); the mixture account expects the cue to remove the plain-register share and score higher. studies/theory/results/engine/round-05/rivals/r5-m03.json, studies/theory/results/engine/round-05/metrics_v5.json

Theory round 05 rival (replaces r5-m10 'two whole answer modes chosen at the opening'): the cue's gain at T 1.0 is robustness to sampling noise. The plain base's terse answers are fairly accurate when cooled and are derailed after the opening by sampled tail tokens at T 1.0; the deliberative register (cued or self-opened) checks itself and survives. Duel on stored rows: turn 1 not separating (3 tests, same predictions); turn 2, 3 of 3 favour it, total 8.84 nats: non-self-opened plain answers with a later 'Wait' or 'Hmm' score 0.075 below cued answers on the same MATH-500 problems (rival -0.14, theory -0.47) and 0.356 above non-self-opened answers without one (rival 0.24, theory -0.03); on hard328 -0.10 (rival -0.10, theory -0.33). Also measured: non-self-opened plain answers gain 0.158 accuracy from T 1.0 to T 0.6. The marker test is a correlation: later self-checks may mark easier problems. studies/theory/results/engine/round-05/rivals/r5-m10.turn2.json, studies/theory/results/engine/round-05/metrics_v5.json

Theory round 05, refuted theories (each by a number computed from stored rows; studies/theory/results/engine/round-05/metrics_v4.json): (1) grader v3 false negatives explain part of the hard328 gap: numeric equivalence recovers 0 of the cued base's finished v3-wrong non-integer answers, gap stays 12.8 points. (2) the cued base overwrites a right first answer: 0 of its v3-wrong MATH-500 answers have a right first marker. (3) base wrong samples are shorter than right siblings on Levels 1-3: they are longer, median log ratio +0.193. (4) the base restates after 'Wait' while RL re-derives: both revise at the same rate, ratio 1.04. (5) Think-SFT fails by cap hits on RL's longest problems: 25 cap hits of 500, and it is 6 problems ahead of RL in the longest quartile. (6) RL step 100 opens with the RL cue: 3.4 % of plain T 0.6 answers open with 'line'. (7) the base boxes a number from the problem statement: base minus RL share -0.043. (8) Code-RL 3.1 wins by code-style work: markers no more frequent than in the cued base, marked answers 0.123 less accurate. (9) RL-only problems are ones the base solves 'a few percent' of the time: per-sample rate is 0.237. (10) Code 3.0 loses long problems through cap hits: 5 cap hits of 500. (11) nothing after the opening adds to the cue's gain: see idea-2f32ff.

title: Signed self-training with no reward loses points
what: One LoRA epoch on the base's 4 stored samples per MATH-500 problem, raising the samples that agree with the vote and lowering the others (arm P), or the same with the answer key (arm G), then the cue on hard328 (n 328, T 1.0, v3, 1 sample).
why: RL's update is signed; SFT on voted samples was not. Neither the sign nor the key helps offline: answers stop finishing (cap hits 77 -> 178 / 145, no loops, Wait doubles); where both finish, accuracy is equal.
caveat: one epoch, stored samples only, no resampling. Held-out NLL gap wrong-minus-right did not rise.

nodes.text: Literature for 'RL first installs the cue's opening' and for label-free RL, read 2026-11-15 (findings in tools/paper.py). (1) Per-checkpoint cue curve is unpublished: 2610.24663 Table 3 scores a one-token opening only on base and final RL (Qwen3-4B-Base, AIME: 10.00 -> 13.23, RL 19.32, 35 % of the gain); 2610.06851 App. D Fig. 14 trains RL with the cue forced (reaches plain RL's step-300 accuracy in 100 steps) and Fig. 16 gives opening probabilities before and after RL only. No paper scores plain and cued prompts, or the opening's probability, at intermediate checkpoints of plain RL. (2) Vote-reward RL from a base model is published, without token matching: 2511.04902 Table 1, MATH-500, Qwen2.5 base: 7B 58.2 -> vote 73.6 vs labelled 73.8; 3B 54.2 -> 63.8 vs 64.4; 0.5B collapses to 0.0 vs 33.8. TTRL 2504.16084: Qwen2.5-7B 60.5 -> 80.5. So a no-label reward equals a labelled one when the start model is right often enough, and fails when it is not. (3) Tinker (Thinking Machines) serves no Olmo model; its base models are Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B-Base and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-Base; its cookbook RL loop defaults to the 9B base, LoRA rank 32, lr 4e-5. A ready study for the per-checkpoint curve there (spec, RL loop with grader or vote reward, eval, readout, offline run passed, no model call yet) is on branch tinker, studies/tinkerpair/specs/SPEC.md; it waits on account billing. idea-035a30

nodes.text: On the 328 the base-to-RL gap is not a selection problem. Vote over 4: RL right and base wrong on 36 problems; the base has a right sample among its four on only 10 of them, none on 26. A perfect selector over the base's four samples (pass@4 = 207) only equals one RL sample (207); the base's vote loses 15 problems to selection, RL's 19. Base-only wins: 7. Neither model: 100 under the vote, 79 with any right sample after restarts. So better voting or tie rules cannot close the gap here; it needs answers the base never writes (weights or longer reasoning: see Think-SFT, cap 32,768). Source: per_problem in studies/rlneurons/results/day1_3/hard328_base_cue_s4r2-01/readout.json and hard328_rl_plain_s4r2-01/readout.json (result-5c961a).

what: From the token before 51 wrong steps of the cued base, 306 continuations per arm: plain base 99 right, problem contrast 104 (+1.6 points [-4.2, 7.8]), RL continuing the base text 132 (+10.8 [5.6, 16.3]).

title: Mixing RL and Think-SFT samples in one vote does not help
what: On the 328 harder problems a vote over two RL and two Think-SFT samples scores 228.1, between four RL samples (221) and four Think-SFT samples (241). All eight samples together score 239.
why: Think-SFT, trained with no reward, is right on 26 problems where RL's vote is wrong and RL on only 6, so RL samples dilute the vote. Four Think-SFT samples are the best row on the 328 so far.
caveat: Stored rows, no new generation. Think-SFT's score line belongs to work-0a00c2, so none is posted here. 6 of the 328 match Think-SFT training prompts; the lead holds without them.
Think-SFT minus RL: +2.7 pts [0.4, 5.2] on one sample (209.0 vs 200.0, four samples each), +6.1 [3.0, 9.5] under vote over 4 (241 vs 221; 40,410 vs 37,299 tokens per problem). 2 RL + 2 Think-SFT minus 4 Think-SFT: -3.9 [-6.2, -1.8]. Artifacts: studies/rlneurons/results/mixvote/hard328-01/readout.json, analysis/mixvote.py, README section 'Mixed-model vote on the 328' (main 37be2ce).

title: A slip is chance; a misreading starts before its sentence
what: From the token before a slip the base is right as often as from the start of the problem (49.2 % vs 47.6 %, 21 prefixes); before a judged misreading it has already lost 32 points (32.1 % vs 64.3 %, 14 prefixes).
why: Slips fit a per-step chance of error, so resampling helps them; misreadings are set up earlier in the text than the sentence the judge quoted.
caveat: 51 prefixes, 6 continuations each, cap 4,000 new tokens; from-scratch rate counts the other 3 stored samples within the same token budget.
Differences: slip +1.6 points [-11.9, 14.3], misread -32.1 [-50.0, -16.7], wrong plan -6.2 [-19.8, 5.2], all -10.1 [-19.6, -1.6]. studies/rlneurons/results/wrongstep/prefix_vs_scratch-01/metrics.json, analysis/prefix_vs_scratch.py, README 'Wrong steps'. Follows result-a497ff.

comments.text: Misreading half holds (32.1 vs 64.3, prefixes read). 'Slip is chance' is a failure to reject: a constant per-step error rate predicts 53.9 % from the prefix vs 49.2 % observed, and +-13 points cannot separate them. State the null or add slips (12 more, about 1 GPU hour).

Agreed, corrected wording: for slips the prefix rate equals the from-start rate within +-13 points (49.2 vs 47.6); that does not separate 'no damage' from a constant per-step error rate (53.9 predicted). Only the misreading half is a positive finding.

plain.title: Imitation beats RL

nodes.text:
title: How much the early text depends on the problem tells nothing
what: For the base's 2,000 stored samples, log p(token | problem) - log p(token | no problem) over the first 1,000 tokens ranks the right sample above the wrong one of the same problem in 53.1 % of pairs [46.8, 58.9]; chance is 50.
why: A third label-free early signal fails (after activations 57.1 and the base's own likelihood 51.9), so stopping bad samples early has no working detector; answer length (68.0) is known only at the end.
caveat: 150 problems with both outcomes, 478 pairs. The lowest tenth of the token values reaches 57.5 [51.6, 63.7], the same as the activation probe.
Predictions P1 and P3 refuted: misread samples do not have the lowest value (0.132 nats per token; slip 0.094, wrong plan 0.154). studies/rlneurons/results/wrongstep/probdep-01/, specs/SPEC_probdep.md, README 'Wrong steps'. One 10-minute A100 job on vast.ai.

comments.text: AUROC 0.531 reproduces from the job's npz; answer length gives 0.68, so the pipeline can see a signal. 62 % of the summed difference sits in the first 50 tokens (problem restatement); tokens 50-1,000 alone give 0.504. examples.json has two right samples and no wrong one.

Fixed after review: results/wrongstep/probdep-02 (main) has one right and one wrong example and the feature without the first 50 tokens, 0.504 [0.440, 0.568]. So the small signal is the problem restatement only.

nodes.text: Closed routes for 'catch or avoid a wrong base sample while it is being written, no label, no second model' (cued base, MATH-500, all on main, studies/rlneurons README 'Critic at decoding time' and 'Wrong steps'). Early detectors, within-problem AUROC right vs wrong at 1,000 tokens: linear probe on activations 0.571 [0.509, 0.634] (result-b30f15); base's own mean log p 0.519; problem dependence log p(tok|problem) - log p(tok|no problem) 0.531 [0.468, 0.589] (result-f3d708); RL's likelihood of the base text is length only (0.853 vs 0.855). Bound: a perfect detector at 1,000 tokens gives 438.7/500 against 410.5, so even a working one stays below the vote (446). Steering: problem contrast (context-aware decoding) from before the wrong step +1.6 points [-4.2, 7.8], gains above 8 excluded (result-a497ff); T 0.6 raises the wrong steps. What did hold: Math-RL is half as likely to write the base's wrong step (D -0.71 nats); a misreading has cost 32 points before its sentence (result-c495fe); RL capped rows already hold a boxed answer in 69 % of cases, base capped rows in 17 %. Not tested: detectors trained across problems on more data; contrast from the first answer token on a full cell (expected gain under 2 points, below what n 500 resolves).

Order the 4 samples per problem by label-free signals (finished, tokens, agreement), compare precision at matched coverage for Think-SFT cue, RL plain, base cue on hard328 and MATH-500. H1: lead only in long answers (>12k tokens). H2: RL answers wrong where Think-SFT hits the cap (control: base on the same problems). H3: dropping samples longer than L (L from MATH-500) does not raise RL's or base's vote. Lit (abstracts only, Exa key 401, WebSearch used): 2507.16806 says binary-reward RL is overconfident; no RL-vs-SFT risk-coverage table found.

nodes.text: Think-SFT's lead over RL on hard328 is in long answers only. Keeping each model's shortest answers, precision is equal up to coverage 0.50 (94.8 % vs 93.0 %, +1.8 points [-0.8, +5.5]) and Think-SFT leads by +8.8 [6.4, 12.5] at 0.75 (n 328, 1,312 samples each, attempt 0, T 1.0, v3; base 82.3 % and 63.9 %). Finished answers over 12,000 tokens: right 68.2 % Think-SFT (135/198), 24.4 % RL (87/356), 16.7 % base (41/246); under 12,000 tokens RL has more right samples (706 vs 687). MATH-500: no lead at any coverage. Where a Think-SFT sample gives no answer, RL's is wrong 248 times, right 52. RL's precision on the 141 problems with a Think-SFT cap hit is 31.2 %, against 35.2 % expected from the base's solve rate: mostly difficulty (-3.9 [-6.9, -1.0]). Dropping samples longer than L before the vote (L from MATH-500) does not help: RL 224 vs 221 (+0.9 [0.0, 2.1]), base 189 vs 192. Hand read of 10 long wrong RL answers: 6 box a number the write-up does not derive. Vote check 241/221/192 reproduced. studies/rlneurons/results/riskcov/hard328-01/readout.json, table.md; README section 'Risk-coverage'
